issues.message: The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.detail: The yard is mostly bare paving with coarse dirt patches; a barrel, a few stone stacks and the grindstone are all that is in it.
notes.purpose: Reads as a walled stone yard with a shed, but the mason's work barely shows yet: no tools, no cut stone laid out, nothing that says 'stone' over 'storage'.
notes.roof: Dark oak eaves do stick out past the long side walls, so the overhang warning is half a false alarm; but the gables are flush with no overhang, the gable fill is plain spruce planks and there is no gable trim.
notes.life: No plants, lanterns or flowers; only coarse dirt.
notes.depth: Dark oak corner posts help, but the long side wall (iso back) and the back gable are flat stone with one window.
notes.materials: Stone brick, cobble, dark oak, spruce: a clean palette.
notes.shape: Shed plus yard with an off-centre gap and stone piles: good asymmetry.

visual.summary: L1 is the shell: an open stone-brick shed under a spruce gable roof inside a low walled, paved yard, with a grindstone, a barrel and rough stone piles.
problems: The yard is too empty for a working stone yard: add a few small things even at L1 (a cut-stone pile of slabs/stairs by the shed door, a stone_button or lever as a mallet on the banker, a lantern on a gate post).
The gables (front and back, z=0 and z=9 side of the roof) have no overhang and no trim: push the roof one block past each gable or add a dark oak stair/trapdoor trim along the verge.
The long side wall of the shed (iso back view) is one flat cobble/stone brick face: break it with a dark oak post or beam in the middle, or a window sill.
Reachability fine: only roof slopes, the ridge and three single wall-top spots are unreached; floor and yard are all reached.

issues.message: The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.detail: Yard is better than v1 (barrel cluster at x=8..9 z=5..6, sledge and half-dressed block at x=1..2 z=2..3, lanterns on the gate piers), but the right half of the yard (x=7..9, z=0..4) is still plain gravel with two coarse dirt patches.
notes.depth: Long side walls (x=1 and x=5) now have a centre glass pane between corner posts over a cobble plinth; still mostly flat at L1 (shutters and corbels only come at L2).
notes.roof: Fixed: roof now overhangs both gables (2 rows at the front z=2..3, 1 at the back z=9) and both eaves (dark oak stairs at x=0 and x=6), with upside-down stair verge trim and a dark oak tie beam and king post on each gable. The automatic 'no overhang' warning is a false alarm.
notes.life: Lanterns and coarse dirt only; no plants at L1.

visual.summary: L1 is the walled stone yard with an open stone brick shed under a spruce gable roof: grindstone, banker, chest, barrels, stone stacks. v2 fixes the gable overhang and trim and partly fills the yard.
problems: Right part of the yard (x=7..9, z=0..4) is still bare gravel: one more small prop there (a slab pile or a barrel) would finish it.
Long side walls at L1 are still flat apart from the centre pane; a sill (stone brick slab/stair under the pane at y=1, z=6) would help.
Reachability fine: only roof slopes, the ridge and three single wall/pier tops are unreached; shed floor and yard all reached.

issues.message: The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.roof: Automatic 'no overhang' warning is a false alarm: the renders show a 2-row front overhang over the bay and eaves past the long walls; half-timbered gables.
notes.detail: Yard has grindstone, bench, barrels, sledge, rough and dressed stone, pier lanterns; side walls still fairly plain at L1, fine for a first build.
notes.artefacts: No floating blocks; pier lanterns stand on stone bricks.
notes.materials: groundLayer 0: layer 0 flush with the grass (noted, not failed).

visual.summary: Level 1: walled stone yard round an open stone brick shed under a spruce gable roof with grindstone, cutting bench, rough and dressed stone; reads clearly as a stonemason's yard.
problems: Minor: long side walls still mostly flat apart from the centre pane at L1; a sill under the pane would add depth.
Reachability fine: only roof slopes, the ridge and three single wall/pier tops (10,2,0), (10,2,9), (5,3,0) unreached; shed floor and yard all reached.
